html:
Brown v. Board of Education was the 1954 ruling in which the US Supreme Court declared racial segregation in public schools unconstitutional.

Since Plessy v. Ferguson in 1896, states could keep Black and white people apart as long as the facilities were "separate but equal". In practice, schools for Black children were poorer in every way. Lawyers of the NAACP, led by Thurgood Marshall, brought several cases together, one of them for a girl named Linda Brown in Topeka, Kansas.

Chief Justice Earl Warren wrote for a unanimous court that separate schools were "inherently unequal".

The ruling did not end segregation by itself. A second decision in 1955 told schools to integrate "with all deliberate speed", and many Southern states resisted for years. In 1957 federal troops had to escort nine Black students into a high school in Little Rock, Arkansas.

Still, Brown gave the civil rights movement law on its side. It was followed by the Montgomery bus boycott, the rise of Martin Luther King Jr., and the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
sum: Brown v. Board of Education was the 1954 ruling in which the US Supreme Court declared racial segregation in public schools unconstitutional.
